title: His Mower Makes Grass LONGER
premise: Our neighbor Mr. Odell mows his lawn at three in the morning with his eyes shut, and the grass comes out longer. The street's rule is never to look while the mower runs, so every blind snaps shut. My dad lives next door to him and has never spoken to him, but Mr. Odell waves at Dad like he misses him, and at a coffee cart he says Dad's order before Dad gives it.
twist: Mr. Odell lives backward through time. Our tomorrow is his yesterday: he isn't guessing Dad's future, he remembers it, and in Dad's future the two of them are best friends. Dad buys two coffees at sunrise, guesses hot chocolate, crosses the fence, and Mr. Odell has ordered that for six years. Dad's guess is the first day of a friendship that, for Mr. Odell, ends today.
world: a bright suburban cul-de-sac at three in the morning: a floodlit straight-striped lawn with a lime yardstick staked in it and a red push mower on an orange cord, a butter yellow house with a blinded upstairs window, a coral house across the street, a low white fence, and by day a teal coffee cart at the curb
